summary.headline: Fratelli Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR36 crores and EBITDA turned near breakeven at INR1.06 crores for FY26, with FY27 guidance of about 30% growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose about 13% YoY to INR36 crores, with gross margin at 79% and EBITDA loss narrowing to INR3.7 crores from INR7 crores a year earlier. For the full year, revenue was nearly flat at INR184 crores (about 1% growth) because of regulatory disruptions in Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttarakhand in H1, and FY EBITDA was INR1 crore. Management said conditions normalised in H2 and that Q1 FY27 momentum continued, and guided to about 30% growth in FY27 with PAT breakeven at roughly INR240 crores of revenue. The RTD brand Shotgun sold about 100,000 cases in its first year.

financial_highlights.value: INR1 crore (positive, stated as INR1.06 crores in opening remarks)

segments.name: Premium & Above (wine)
segments.commentary: Contributes more than 70% of overall revenue per the CEO, and more than 40% per the CFO-side Q&A; premium segment revenue declined about 15-16% YoY in FY26 due to H1 regulatory disruptions. Growth was seen in Haryana, UP, Kerala and Sikkim.

segments.name: Luxury (above INR2,000 MRP)
segments.commentary: Sales grew 15% YoY in FY26; flagship J'NOON grew 44%. Management claims more than 50% domestic luxury wine market share.

segments.name: RTD (Shotgun)
segments.commentary: Launched in H1 FY26, about 100,000 cases sold in year one, about INR18 crores revenue, present in 18 states and about 9,000 outlets (2,000 added in the year). Target is to double sales in FY27; marketing spend above 10% of its revenue.

segments.name: CSD channel
segments.commentary: About 8% of overall revenue, with about 45% market share. Merlot and NOI received approvals with sales from H1 FY27; Shotgun expected from H2 FY27.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue doubled in FY26 across 15 countries; management expects exports at 5% of total revenue from FY27. Q4 export business more than doubled YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 30%, which management equated to about INR240 crores of revenue and net-net (PAT) breakeven.
Management expects growth to show from Q1 FY27 versus the prior year.
FY27 capex guided at INR6-10 crores (also cited as about INR9 crores for routine and strategic capex); no major capex commitments expected beyond that.
Hospitality project (INR70-80 crores) deferred by about a year; review in H2 FY26-27 with action possibly in calendar 2027-28.
Gross margin expected to settle in a 76-80% range as RTD (margins near 70%) grows; marketing spend guided at about 7% of revenue normally.
Long-term aspiration of about INR500 crores revenue by 2030 at 20% CAGR was referenced in Q&A.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about INR10 crores across vineyard infrastructure, plant and machinery and operational infrastructure; major capex cycle described as largely complete.
Infrastructure built is expected to support growth for about 3 years.
FY27 capex expected at INR6-10 crores; hospitality project estimated at INR70-80 crores, now deferred.
Vineyards are company-owned with drip irrigation, and management said it is comfortable on El Nino rainfall risk.
Shotgun distribution expected to exceed 15,000 outlets by around H2 FY27 from about 9,000 now; Shotgun to launch in Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Telangana in H1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management said discounts and schemes have stayed fairly consistent for 2-3 years and it is working to reduce them.
Management says the wine RTD market is about INR500-600 crores, growing about 25% YoY, and that the segment's price band is INR150-200.
FTA impact: management says more than 90% of wine revenue is below INR2,000 MRP and sees no major impact on pricing or volume from the India-EU FTA in the near term.

Sette expansion: 7 more states in FY27 (Delhi, Haryana, UP, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra) after 5 states at launch. Fratelli Brut (INR1,500) is in 4 states, with 14 more states planned for FY27.
Company says it has about 200 people in sales and marketing and uses Salesforce; HoReCa market share is close to 40%.
Market share: about 30% in premium wine and more than 50% in domestic luxury wine (per management).

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to PAT profitability and key milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about 30% growth in FY27 with operating efficiencies, which it expects to deliver PAT breakeven for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the RTD market and how is consumer adoption evolving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the wine RTD market at about INR500-600 crores growing about 25% YoY; the market is over 1 million cases and Fratelli's target is to double to over 200,000 cases in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin path to 20% EBITDA, and which cost lines will save?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating leverage will come from scale, with costs already set up to double revenue without major change; the hospitality business is not expected to drive cost efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Net-net breakeven scale for PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net-net breakeven comes at about INR240 crores of revenue, which the 30% growth target would reach in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the marketing spend guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal guidance is about 7% of top line; Shotgun has been above 10% in year one and is expected to stay above 10% this year, with spend higher in the first three years.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the India-EU FTA on pricing and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no major pricing or volume impact is seen in the foreseeable future and that the impact will be clearer over the next year.

risks_watch: Regulatory and excise disruptions in key states (Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Delhi) hit premium volumes in H1 FY26; Q1 FY27 recovery needs to be tracked.
The 30% FY27 growth guidance is a large step-up from about 1% in FY26; watch quarterly revenue for evidence.
Shotgun's outlet ramp (9,000 to 15,000+) and the CSD launches depend on state registrations.
Marketing spend above 10% for Shotgun and rising costs (employee and other expenses, depreciation, finance costs) could keep EBITDA margins below the 20% target.
Hospitality project timing is open; cost is INR70-80 crores and management has not committed to a date.
Management did not disclose a precise PAT figure or the FY26 EBITDA margin; the INR1 crore versus INR1.06 crore figures differ slightly.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the recovery and FY27 growth outlook, but vague on specifics: it declined to detail cost lines, could not quantify the overall market share, and answered some questions only partially. Management was also clearly keen to frame RTD as the second growth engine.
key_quotes: Encouragingly, market conditions began to normalize during the second half of the year, and we witnessed a meaningful pickup in sales.
So add around INR240 crores is when we get to a net-net breakeven.
Our cost structure is now more or less geared up for even doubling the business from today.
